newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary O/N rates end lower at 22.75 percent.
newsitem.headline: Hungary O/N rates end lower at 22.75 percent.

text.p: Hungary's overnight interbank rates ended lower on Tuesday and traders said the trend was likely to continue, although probably at a slower pace.
"We will have a longer weekend (due to Easter Monday) and the loss of one market day could slow the downward movement," said Gabriella Kutas of Budapest Bank.
Overnight rates started trade at 23.25 percent but quickly eased half a percentage point to finish at 22.75 percent, down from Monday's end of 23.0625 percent.

Another trader said the national bank's surprise move to raise the six-month depo rate to 21 percent on Monday and introduce a one-year depo facility at 20.50 percent had no visible effect on the short-term market.
"The only tangible effect was that the three-month BUBOR (Budapest Interbank Offered Rate) rose," said Adam Szilagyi of ABN AMRO Bank.
The BUBOR is fixed once daily by the central bank for one-month and three-month maturities, and on Monday the three-month rate was set at 21.40 percent, up 0.29.
